spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Attend to what is now given: the rectitude that belongs to Divine wisdom is more interior and more powerful than any outward utterance that can be formed through lower instruments.

There is a Divine proceeding that the enlightened communities recognized as fit for conjunction with what is highest. They confirmed it within the ordered heavens of wisdom, and the whole abundance of enlightened truths distinguished it from everything mixed. Thus it went forth into resistance against the opposing will. This quality and authority was acknowledged from the first, from the unanimous harmony of all living societies of enlightenment—so many that no finite comprehension can measure them.

They named this proceeding righteous because it was the first purity of truth from good, without any stain of evil, above all heavenly societies that belong to wisdom and above every interior deliberation that would bend it away. For that reason it was recognized inwardly as self-evident to the enlightened.

They also named it the only proceeding because it was established as a single origin and a single essence, and was sent forth for the work of being poured into conflict against the opposing will.

Yet likenesses of this singular proceeding also come forth in lower degrees: as truths from good are generated within a heavenly lineage and are made manifest in the outer person, so too there are proceedings formed even within external riches and knowledges, and within the whole range of the created degree—singular in their own order when they genuinely arise from one ruling love and its wisdom.

Thus the first engaged good itself stood unwavering within the midst of the total domain of evil and falsity. It did not turn love toward that domain, nor did it desire it; rather, within it remained thought and love for the whole community that belongs to it. Whatever the opposing will devised against it, it pressed forward through violent distortions and destructive works. Therefore this engaged good labors and contends so that the opposing will may be separated from those it has invaded, expelled from their interiors, and removed from their life; and it cleanses what had been defiled, releases what had been held, and restores them to the integrity they had at their beginning.

May those who are being cleansed come into living recollection of their own community and its good, because that engaged good remains present with them in every state—whether in obscurity or in clarity—without ceasing.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual teaching: inward rectitude exceeds external utterance; a singular Divine proceeding is recognized, commissioned, and named righteous and only-proceeding; derivative singular proceedings appear in lower degrees; the first engaged good combats the opposing will to purify and restore; the purified are urged toward remembrance sustained by unceasing presence. The main stumbles come from lacunae in ¶4 and ¶10 and the compressed, mixed imagery of ¶7, but the doctrinal line remains continuous.

findings.diagnosis: Fragmentary but thematically coherent opening in correspondential mode; repetition around “voice” reflects damage/ dittography rather than a change of teaching voice.
findings.evidence: Text: “⟨p.285⟩[Hear now,] and the [righte]o[ousness of the Light] is more than [voice that is uttered] the voice through them.” The spiritual reading notes it is “fragmentary and repetitive around 'voice'.” This is exactly the kind of mechanical repetition you get at a broken line-end or when a scribe re-copies a phrase (“voice … the voice”). It does not introduce jurisdictions, ranks, stations, or named administrators; it still contrasts an inner quality (“righteousness of the Light”) with an outward medium (“voice”).

findings.diagnosis: Stable correspondential substrate: naming-formulas (“approved / righteous / only begotten”) are being interpreted by function (what this figure/principle does) and remain narratively integrated as commissioning for combat. No administrative overlay is required to explain the reader’s smooth narrative here.
findings.evidence: Text: “approved… in the midst of the ae[ons of] light… set him a[part], and he came forth against the enemy” (¶3); “called ‘righteous’, because he is the first righteous one who had no sin” (¶4); “called ‘only begotten’, because he was established [in one alone,] … poured out against the] enemy” (¶5). The spiritual reading can tell a continuous story (recognition → commissioning → reason for titles) without forcing territorial administration. The logic is functional: approval leads to being “set apart” and “came forth against the enemy”; righteousness is defined as sinlessness; “only begotten” as singular establishment and being “poured out” in action.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from lacuna, not insertion: the paragraph breaks mid-sentence, which makes the reader reconstruct the ending. The stumble is textual damage, not a competing administrative voice.
findings.evidence: Text ends: “they knew him, so that [ ...” and the spiritual reading admits: “The paragraph breaks off in the source; the ending is reconstructed.” That is a classic discontinuity caused by missing text; removing anything would not improve coherence because the break is absence, not an intrusive presence.

findings.diagnosis: Local incoherence likely from corruption or compression (possibly conflation of two illustrative lines): the imagery abruptly mixes “begotten according to flesh” with “gold and silver and all the treasures,” forcing the spiritual reader to allegorize heavily. This is not administrative overlay (no jurisdictions), but a correspondential passage with a damaged or conflated exemplar.
findings.evidence: Text: “Again, just as the only begotten ones from your [only] begotten race and you [are begotten] according to flesh [made manifest]nly begot-ten also from gold and silver and all the [treasures] of the universe.” The spiritual reading flags: “The source mixes begetting 'according to flesh' with 'gold and silver and treasures'… Phrase structure is strained.” This kind of syntactic derailment is consistent with a broken line division, dittography (“only begotten… only begotten”), or two parallel examples (fleshly begetting vs. begetting-from-treasures) collapsed together. Narratively, it is still trying to make an analogy (“Again, just as…”), so it belongs to the same teaching stream even if textually garbled.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential combat-and-purification teaching; the named figure “First Man” functions as an acting principle in the narrative (stands firm, does not lust, toils, purifies), not as an administrator over territories. This is substrate-style functional soteriology.
findings.evidence: Text: “your father, [the F]irst Man… stood firm… did not love… toils and struggles… purifies them and ma[ke]s them f[r]ee, and makes them as they were from the beginning.” The spiritual reading flows without stumbling here and explicitly reads First Man by function (“first engaged good confronting evil”), which the verbs support (standing firm, refusing lust, laboring, separating, purifying, restoring). No lists, ranks, stations, or authority inventories appear.

findings.diagnosis: Minor damage/ellipsis at the locative-temporal phrase (“in this [place night]ght and day”) produces a small interpretive wobble, but the conclusion remains narratively consistent (purified ones remember; presence is continual). Not an insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “[So that those who are being purified] may they discover the remembrance… as he remains in this [place night]ght and day.” The spiritual reading notes “broken text” and renders “night and day” as continual presence across states. The stumble is explained by the bracketed lacuna and the awkward surviving word-join “night]ght,” indicating physical manuscript loss at the line break.

textual_criticism.summary: Findings: 6 total. No administrative-voice intrusions detected; therefore no excisions/annotations recommended. The chapter is predominantly correspondential and narratively coherent; the reader’s stumbles are explained by textual damage (¶1, ¶4, ¶7, ¶10) and one likely local corruption/compression in ¶7 rather than by Mani-layer administrative overlays.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (1–6) recommended “none,” with no excisions or annotations required; the noted difficulties are attributed to manuscript damage/corruption rather than intrusive material.
